title: AWS ECS Task Placement Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `eventSource="ecs.amazonaws.com" (eventName="RunTask" OR eventName="CreateService")` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.1.57 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `eventSource="ecs.amazonaws.com" (eventName="RunTask" OR eventName="CreateService")`. Confirm UC-4.1.57 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="ecs.amazonaws.com" (eventName="RunTask" OR eventName="CreateService")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.57_aws_ecs_task_placement_f_57"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.1.57 — AWS ECS Task Placement Failures: queries AWS `aws:cloudtrail` for `RunTask`, `CreateService` and returns actor, resource, and region context for availability review and change validation.
value: On AWS, `RunTask` activity for 'AWS ECS Task Placement Failures' is a high-signal control-plane change that should match approved change records and privileged-access monitoring. UC-4.1.57 drives high-priority availability alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: CloudTrail logs ECS API calls; RunTask and CreateService responses include a `failures` array when placement fails. Ingest ECS events from EventBridge for container instance state changes. Parse failure reasons (RESOURCE:MEMORY, RESOURCE:CPU, RESOURCE:PORT, attribute constraints). Alert on any placement failure. Dashboard by cluster, reason, and task definition. Remediate by adding capacity, relaxing constraints, or adjusting task definitions.
visualization: Table (reason, cluster, count), Bar chart (failures by reason), Timeline (placement failure events).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` max(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as peak
  from datamodel=Performance.All_Performance
  by Performance.object Performance.host span=1h
| where isnotnull(peak)
| sort - peak
dataModelAcceleration: Performance: enable if `aws:cloudwatch` (or your metric store) is mapped to CIM Performance, or use `mstats` on the same CloudWatch metrics. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Planned deploys, game-day tests, and vendor maintenance that you expect to move CPU, error, or lag metrics; compare with the change window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
CloudTrail logs ECS API calls; RunTask and CreateService responses include a `failures` array when placement fails. Ingest ECS events from EventBridge for container instance state changes. Parse failure reasons (RESOURCE:MEMORY, RESOURCE:CPU, RESOURCE:PORT, attribute constraints). Alert on any placement failure. Dashboard by cluster, reason, and task definition. Remediate by adding capacity, relaxing constraints, or adjusting task definitions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventSource="ecs.amazonaws.com" (eventName="RunTask" OR eventName="CreateService")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.57_aws_ecs_task_placement_f_57"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect aws ecs task placement failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_57_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (reason, cluster, count), Bar chart (failures by reason), Timeline (placement failure events)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of aws ecs task placement failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
